hirebotics.title: Hirebotics adds line tracking and linear rails to extend cobot capabilities
hirebotics.summary: New features help cobots paint moving parts and reach larger workpieces, bringing more flexibility to production lines.

sections.heading: Moving parts and larger workpieces
paragraphs: Hirebotics introduced line tracking for conveyor-based painting and a modular linear rail at IMTS 2026 in Chicago. Both use the Beacon platform as their main interface, extending the range of tasks its cobots can handle.

sections.heading: Painting without stopping the conveyor
paragraphs: Sensors detect the workpiece and an encoder tracks conveyor movement. The system adjusts the painting path as the part moves. Operators teach the direction and configure the task in Beacon; the company says conventional programming is not required.

sections.heading: Extending the working envelope
paragraphs: The cobot has a reach of about 1.75 metres. Rail sections add roughly 1.5 metres at a time, with custom lengths also available. This can help with long structures or difficult-to-move parts in welding, plasma cutting and painting applications.

sections.heading: Available features and future plans
paragraphs: At the time of publication, operators repositioned the rail manually. Hirebotics planned to add position confirmation in Beacon and targeted automatic rail movement for late 2026. Those planned capabilities should be distinguished from features already available.

locus.title: Locus Robotics and Kimball Midwest win supply-chain robotics award
locus.summary: A deployment across three distribution centres has supported more than 13.2 million picks, with the companies reporting productivity gains and payback within a year.

sections.heading: Recognition for a working warehouse deployment
paragraphs: Locus Robotics and Kimball Midwest received the Best Use of Robotics award at the 2026 Supply Chain Excellence Awards USA. The project started in Columbus in January 2024 and expanded to three sites within 14 months without major changes to existing shelving.

sections.heading: A fleet of more than 100 robots
paragraphs: Autonomous mobile robots support picking and putaway at distribution centres in Ohio, Texas and Nevada. According to the companies, the deployment has supported more than 13.2 million robot-assisted picks and approximately one million putaway transactions.

sections.heading: Productivity and payback
paragraphs: Picking rates rose from around 110 to more than 160 lines per hour, while putaway increased from about 30 to 91–96 lines per hour. The companies report payback within a year, shorter employee training and less reliance on temporary labour.

sections.heading: Moving staff between changing priorities
paragraphs: Using the same platform for both picking and putaway allows staff to move between tasks as demand changes. The aim is to support growth while maintaining the promise to ship orders received before 4 p.m. on the same day.

abz.title: ABZ Innovation opens a larger European drone factory
abz.summary: The new Szentendre facility in Hungary expands manufacturing for agricultural spraying, industrial cleaning and transport drones.

sections.heading: A new manufacturing base in Hungary
paragraphs: ABZ Innovation opened a facility in Szentendre around four times the size of its previous factory. The company aims to triple output in 2026 and double it again in 2027 as it responds to commercial drone demand.

sections.heading: Four product families
paragraphs: The range comprises L-Series spraying drones, S-Series seed and granular-material spreaders, C-Series high-pressure cleaning drones and M-Series multipurpose transport drones. The company reports deployments in more than 40 countries across six continents.

sections.heading: Production and after-sales support
paragraphs: The facility is intended to serve as a global manufacturing hub. ABZ emphasises European production, data control, training, spare parts and after-sales service for customers who use drones in their day-to-day operations.

sections.heading: The expansion behind the announcement
paragraphs: The investment follows a €7 million funding round in January 2026. ABZ says industrial cleaning is its fastest-growing product line. Its production targets remain plans whose eventual delivery will need to be assessed.

light.title: Control ambient light before tuning a robotic inspection camera
light.summary: Windows, overhead fixtures and nearby work areas can change inspection images. The lighting environment needs attention before camera settings are finalised.

sections.heading: External light makes images inconsistent
paragraphs: EVST recommends checking windows, overhead lighting and adjacent work areas before adjusting an inspection camera. Light that changes during the day can make settings that work at one time unreliable at another.

sections.heading: Start with the real inspection cell
paragraphs: The accompanying video shows a part inside a cell with transparent panels and a window behind it, while a local light moves with the end device. This illustrates the layout but does not establish image quality or defect-detection accuracy.

sections.heading: Match light control to its source
paragraphs: The article discusses panels or enclosures, short light pulses and optical filters. Each measure should be linked to the source it addresses, including reflections from guarding and the workpiece itself.

sections.heading: Test under changing conditions
paragraphs: When a light or camera moves with the robot, shielding effectiveness can vary with position. Images need to be checked at times with different levels of interfering light before the inspection view can be treated as reliable.

a3.title: A3 adds the business case for automation to its robotics course
a3.summary: A new investment-assessment module helps learners decide where industrial robotics can create value and how to evaluate a project.

sections.heading: Connecting robotics with business decisions
paragraphs: The Association for Advancing Automation, or A3, added a business-case module to its Introduction to Industrial Robotics course. It is intended to help learners identify where automation is appropriate and assess the value of a proposed investment.

sections.heading: Designed for newcomers
paragraphs: The self-paced course does not require a technical background. It is aimed at people entering the field, operations staff and others involved in business decisions about deploying robotics.

sections.heading: Looking beyond the robot purchase price
paragraphs: The new material covers project costs, returns and payback periods, opportunities to improve productivity and quality, and workforce implications. It also addresses early project planning, requests for proposals and selecting an integrator.

sections.heading: Applying the ideas to a real project
paragraphs: Learners can use A3’s Robot System Value Calculator to assess a system they are considering. The central idea is to begin with the problem that needs solving and then examine how technology could deliver a return.

digit.title: From Cassie to Digit 5: Agility Robotics’ path to workplace robots
digit.summary: Agility’s robot generations trace a shift from bipedal locomotion research to practical warehouse work, safety and production readiness.

sections.heading: From walking research to useful work
paragraphs: Agility Robotics began with Cassie, which took its first steps in 2016 and focused on bipedal movement. The first Digit followed in 2017 for researchers. The development path reflects a shift from walking performance to tasks that businesses need done.

sections.heading: Digit reaches commercial applications
paragraphs: Digit 3 in 2019 targeted package delivery and box handling, with a lifting capacity of about 18 kilograms. Ford bought the first two robots to explore deliveries from a vehicle to a doorstep. Digit 4, introduced in 2023, focused on warehouses and distribution centres.

sections.heading: Workplace lessons inform Digit 5
paragraphs: The fifth generation changes the leg structure to favour force over speed and updates the battery and systems for operating near people. According to Agility, the robot assesses risk and slows down or stops when a person approaches.

sections.heading: Company scale and plans
paragraphs: The report describes a workforce of more than 400 and a factory capable of producing up to 10,000 robots per year. That figure is capacity, not actual deliveries. It also discusses a proposed SPAC transaction that had not been completed at the time of reporting.

gen7.title: Universal Robots introduces its AI-ready Gen 7 platform
gen7.summary: The new generation combines PolyScope X, updated robot arms, controllers and teaching interfaces for industrial automation.

sections.heading: A platform-wide update
paragraphs: Universal Robots introduced its seventh-generation platform at IMTS, with PolyScope X at its core. The update spans the controller, teach pendant and tool connections to support industrial applications that use AI.

sections.heading: New arms and controller hardware
paragraphs: The g-Series includes UR10g-1750, UR17g-1300 and UR18g-950 arms, with the names indicating payload and reach. Universal Robots says its CB7 Core controller provides 40% more processing power in a package 30% smaller, with support for multiple factory networks.

sections.heading: Connections for vision and AI
paragraphs: The tool flange provides data, power and connections needed for cameras and sensors. Force and torque sensing, APIs and ROS2 communication are intended to help integrators develop additional applications.

sections.heading: Making teaching easier
paragraphs: The TP7 Core pendant is more than 20% lighter, while the SP7 Smart Panel supports teaching close to the task. More than 20 partners contributed demonstrations. Users still need to select hardware and software suited to each application.

perciva.title: Teledyne e2v adds Perciva ToF to its 3D imaging range
perciva.summary: The new industrial depth camera combines a Hydra3D+ sensor and onboard processing for robotics, logistics and inspection.

sections.heading: Industrial depth sensing
paragraphs: Teledyne e2v introduced Perciva ToF for applications that need depth information, including logistics, robotics and inspection. The camera brings the sensor and processing together in a single device.

sections.heading: The Hydra3D+ sensor
paragraphs: Perciva uses an 832 × 600-pixel Hydra3D+ CMOS sensor with HiRho technology. The manufacturer says its pixel design supports near-infrared sensitivity and low-reflectivity materials while reducing imaging problems with fast-moving objects.

sections.heading: Ready-to-use data over GigE
paragraphs: Factory calibration and onboard processing allow the camera to deliver depth maps and 3D point clouds directly over GigE. This is intended to simplify integration for developers and system integrators.

sections.heading: Demonstrations and supporting information
paragraphs: The announcement says Teledyne plans to demonstrate the camera at VISION in Stuttgart on 6–8 October 2026 and offers documentation or product samples on request. The performance statements are manufacturer claims rather than independent tests in this report.

coating.title: Define coating requirements before configuring a painting robot
coating.summary: Corners, recesses, rear surfaces and suspension points need explicit requirements before a robot’s spray path can be assessed.

sections.heading: Specify each surface region
paragraphs: EVST recommends separate coating requirements for broad surfaces, corners, recesses, rear faces and hanging points. A single description of the desired finish for the whole part can leave important areas undefined.

sections.heading: Motion footage does not prove coating quality
paragraphs: The video shows a robot approaching a suspended part, but cannot establish film thickness or coverage outside the camera’s view. Contact points with the hanging fixture may have different permitted exceptions for different products.

sections.heading: Separate general principles from actual settings
paragraphs: Spray angle and nozzle distance affect coverage, but example settings from other spraying methods should not be transferred directly to a robot. The installed nozzle and actual system must be considered.

sections.heading: Test the unresolved requirement
paragraphs: If the question concerns a deep recess, a front-face inspection will not answer it. Tests need to match the location under review and the real hanging orientation. Validating the robot path and assessing coating quality are separate steps.

images.caption: The view does not establish coating coverage behind the part or at support contacts. Image: EVST.

softbank.title: SoftBank agrees to acquire the Robotics and AI Institute
softbank.summary: The reported agreement would bring Marc Raibert’s research institute into SoftBank’s robotics portfolio, subject to review.

sections.heading: An agreement still under review
paragraphs: The Robot Report says SoftBank agreed to buy the Robotics and AI Institute from Hyundai. Financial terms were not disclosed. The transaction was undergoing CFIUS review, with the precise review status unclear at the time of reporting.

sections.heading: Marc Raibert’s research institute
paragraphs: Based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, RAI was founded in 2022 with more than $400 million in initial investment from Hyundai. Its work spans control, perception, manipulation, navigation and AI for physical tasks.

sections.heading: An existing relationship in robotics
paragraphs: Marc Raibert founded both Boston Dynamics and RAI. SoftBank owned Boston Dynamics from 2017 to 2021 before Hyundai acquired a controlling stake, connecting the organisations through a longer history in robotics.

sections.heading: Questions that remain open
paragraphs: Raibert’s role after a completed deal was unclear. The report suggests RAI’s research could complement SoftBank’s robotics and AI portfolio, but the outcome still depends on approval and subsequent implementation.

birotor.title: Two birotor robots join forces as a four-propeller aerial platform
birotor.summary: IEEE Spectrum’s weekly video collection features connected flying robots alongside humanoids, unusual locomotion and automated laboratories.

sections.heading: A weekly collection of robotics videos
paragraphs: IEEE Spectrum’s Video Friday gathers demonstrations from multiple research and development teams. A highlight is a pair of connected two-propeller flying robots from CLIMB Lab, alongside developments in humanoids and automation.

sections.heading: Movement and working near people
paragraphs: The collection includes Digit 5 and work from Figure, as well as NYU’s WorMa. That robot transfers water between its front and rear to shift its weight distribution and help it negotiate obstacles.

sections.heading: A broad range of research
paragraphs: Other projects include an underwater quadruped, MIT’s automated optics laboratory and NASA’s Lunabotics competition, where students test robotic vehicles in simulated lunar-surface conditions.

sections.heading: How to read the collection
paragraphs: This is a set of videos from different projects, rather than a test of one product. Technical details and experimental results should be checked against the development teams and materials referenced by the original article.

anscer.title: ANSCER reports conditional FCC approval for three mobile robots
anscer.summary: The company says its AR250, AR650 and AR1250 models received conditional approval as it works toward US market access.

sections.heading: Three models named in the announcement
paragraphs: ANSCER Robotics says the AR250, AR650 and AR1250 received conditional FCC approval effective 18 September 2026. The report is a company announcement distributed through RoboticsTomorrow.

sections.heading: What it means for US operations
paragraphs: According to the announcement, the approval allows the company to pursue the equipment authorisations needed for US import and sales, subject to domestic manufacturing and supply-chain transparency conditions.

sections.heading: The approval remains conditional
paragraphs: The announcement distinguishes conditional approval from unconditional equipment authorisation and ties it to manufacturing commitments and continuing reporting. It should not be interpreted as an exemption from all requirements.

sections.heading: Applications for the robots
paragraphs: The AR family moves materials in warehouses, factories and intralogistics operations. The parent company is based in Bengaluru, India, while its Plano, Texas operation handles North American sales and service.

cassie.title: Tutor Intelligence introduces the next generation of Cassie and Sonny
cassie.summary: The company combines updated robot hardware and AI for case handling and individual-item picking in warehouses.

sections.heading: Tutor Intelligence’s robots
paragraphs: MassRobotics shared news of Tutor Intelligence’s next-generation Cassie and Sonny, covering hardware, AI models and deployments. This Cassie is Tutor’s robot, not Agility Robotics’ biped of the same name.

sections.heading: Cassie gains mobility on the factory floor
paragraphs: Cassie is a single-arm robot on a wheeled base for case picking, depalletising and stacking. The company says the new version can travel between stations autonomously, has an integrated vacuum system and adds two 3D LiDAR units for environmental sensing.

sections.heading: Sonny targets individual-item picking
paragraphs: Sonny uses a form focused on human-like dexterity and is intended to use the 4.5-billion-parameter Ti0 vision-language-action model. Initial tasks include warehouse navigation, shelf picking and delivering orders to packing stations.

sections.heading: Business model and claims
paragraphs: Tutor offers usage-based pricing and says the new robots have already been deployed at US facilities. Claims about deployment speed and returns come from the developer and do not guarantee the same results at every warehouse.

marines.title: US Marines share footage of drone training
marines.summary: The footage shows training with Skydio X2D reconnaissance drones and a separate exercise using heavy-lift drones for medical supplies.

sections.heading: Bringing drones into regular units
paragraphs: DroneDJ reports on US Marine Corps training with Skydio X2D drones. The footage reflects efforts to build drone skills in regular units rather than relying solely on specialist teams.

sections.heading: The small-drone operator role
paragraphs: The article discusses the sUAS Operator role, with trained personnel returning to share skills with their home units. It describes the X2D as a small reconnaissance drone equipped with visible-light and thermal imaging.

sections.heading: An example of medical logistics
paragraphs: A separate video from an August exercise shows a heavy-lift drone delivering medical supplies to a simulated casualty-care location. It illustrates a logistics and medical-support application for drones.

sections.heading: Image and video sources
paragraphs: The report references two DVIDS videos and credits images to the US Marine Corps. These depict training exercises as described by the source, not combat operations during an actual incident.

amazon-greenwood-manufacturing-investmen.title: Amazon plans a $100 million-plus factory to support its robotics network
amazon-greenwood-manufacturing-investmen.summary: The Greenwood, Indiana facility will combine fabrication, robotic welding, coating and assembly, with a planned 2028 launch and 300 jobs.

sections.heading: A factory for the fulfillment network
paragraphs: Amazon announced on September 24 that it plans to invest more than $100 million in a roughly 585,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana. It will supply the North American fulfillment and robotics network, with a launch expected by 2028.

sections.heading: Several processes under one roof
paragraphs: Planned capabilities include fabrication, robotic welding, automated powder coating and assembly, supported by AWS, AI manufacturing systems and robotics. The announcement does not identify a particular robot model that the facility will manufacture.

sections.heading: Manufacturing and engineering jobs
paragraphs: Amazon expects 300 manufacturing and engineering positions, including CNC operators, welders, coating technicians, assemblers and controls engineers. The project combines automation investment with the people needed to operate and maintain production.

sections.heading: An announced investment, not an operating plant
paragraphs: The facility and opening date remain plans. The accompanying images and video illustrate Amazon’s existing robotics work. The Indiana project is separate from the Texas manufacturing investment announced earlier.

anymal-secure-door-access-whitegate-2026.title: ANYmal gains secure door access for industrial inspection
anymal-secure-door-access-whitegate-2026.summary: ANYbotics, dormakaba and LEGIC tested automated access at Whitegate power station, combining robot credentials with existing site permissions.

sections.heading: Removing a route barrier
paragraphs: ANYbotics, dormakaba and LEGIC are enabling ANYmal to pass through industrial doors, including access-controlled areas. The aim is to extend inspection routes without staff opening doors, while retaining the site’s safety barriers.

sections.heading: Two access mechanisms
paragraphs: At unlocked doors, radar triggers a dormakaba ED 100 or ED 250 operator. For locked doors, LEGIC digital credentials let the exos access system check authorization before unlocking. Operators can restrict permissions by zone, time window and task.

sections.heading: Tested in an operating power station
paragraphs: The companies report several weeks of testing at GE Vernova’s Whitegate power station in County Cork, Ireland. ANYmal requested access, crossed controlled doors and completed inspection routes without manual intervention in those steps, with timestamped records for auditing.

sections.heading: Existing security still matters
paragraphs: The system does not replace measures against people following an authorized user through a door. Existing site protections remain necessary. The access-control add-on is planned for later in 2026 for installed systems and future ANYmal hardware.

agility-confirms-wheeled-robot-explorati.title: Agility confirms early exploration of wheeled robots
agility-confirms-wheeled-robot-explorati.summary: Jonathan Hurst says the Digit developer is studying additional form factors. The wheeled design remains exploratory, with no product or launch date confirmed.

sections.heading: A new confirmation after the Digit 5 video
paragraphs: The Robot Report asked Jonathan Hurst about a wheeled robot rendering near the end of the Digit 5 launch video. His email confirmed that Agility is exploring several designs, including wheels. The new development is that confirmation, rather than another announcement of Digit 5.

sections.heading: Matching the form to the environment
paragraphs: Hurst said alternative approaches could bring robots to more environments sooner. The report contrasts wheels’ suitability for predictable, flat surfaces with the usefulness of legs around stairs, obstacles and uneven terrain.

sections.heading: No product definition yet
paragraphs: Asked whether this would be a wheeled Digit or a differently named and shaped robot, Hurst said it was too early to say and the work was just starting. Specifications, payload, reach, pricing and a market launch have not been confirmed.

sections.heading: A rendering is not a deployed prototype
paragraphs: The illustration comes from the existing launch video. It does not establish that a commercially ready wheeled prototype exists. Target tasks, physical testing and a decision to turn the exploration into a product remain developments to watch.

asi-softbank-construction-joint-venture-.title: ASI and SoftBank form an autonomous construction joint venture
asi-softbank-construction-joint-venture-.summary: The venture targets mixed-brand equipment coordinated through Mobius. SoftBank also invested $225 million in ASI separately from the venture.

sections.heading: A venture for commercial expansion
paragraphs: ASI announced a joint venture with SoftBank Group to develop and commercialize autonomous construction equipment for large infrastructure projects. SoftBank is capitalizing the venture, but the announcement does not disclose that investment amount.

sections.heading: The $225 million is separate
paragraphs: SoftBank also invested $225 million in ASI to expand its commercial operations in construction. That investment is separate from the joint venture and should not be presented as the venture’s disclosed budget.

sections.heading: Coordinating mixed fleets
paragraphs: ASI’s Mobius platform is intended to coordinate equipment from different manufacturers, including haul trucks, dozers, loaders and compactors. Target applications include civil construction and material handling for infrastructure such as roads, airports and railways.

sections.heading: Deployment details remain open
paragraphs: The release describes the business expansion and platform capabilities, but does not identify a committed machine count, specific venture customers or a delivery timetable. Cost and productivity outcomes will need evidence from actual deployments.

leopard-lumotive-sirius-max-launch-2026.title: Sirius Max combines color and depth with programmable beam steering
leopard-lumotive-sirius-max-launch-2026.summary: Leopard Imaging and Lumotive introduced an RGB-D module for robotics, claiming depth sensing beyond 20 meters and one-megapixel depth resolution.

sections.heading: An integrated perception module
paragraphs: Leopard Imaging and Lumotive introduced Sirius Max, combining RGB imaging, indirect time-of-flight depth sensing and processing for robots and automation. The module is intended to supply synchronized color and depth information in real time.

sections.heading: Software controls where light goes
paragraphs: Lumotive’s TX10 transmitter and LCM technology steer illumination toward software-selected regions. The developers describe a fully solid-state design without moving mechanical parts, allowing sensing priorities to change instead of relying on fixed flood illumination.

sections.heading: One connection for imaging and control
paragraphs: The module uses an onsemi AF0130 depth sensor and GMSL2 to carry synchronized RGB video, depth and control over a coaxial cable. Proposed uses include navigation, mapping, cliff detection, collision avoidance and object handling.

sections.heading: Performance remains a manufacturer claim
paragraphs: Lumotive reports iToF operation beyond 20 meters indoors and outdoors with one-megapixel depth resolution. The announcement does not provide independent benchmarks, pricing or a delivery date. Performance still needs assessment with the actual materials, lighting and motion of a deployment.

ifr-world-robotics-2026-five-million.title: IFR reports five million industrial robots operating worldwide
ifr-world-robotics-2026-five-million.summary: World Robotics 2026 puts 2025 installations above 600,000, with China accounting for 59% and the United States becoming the second-largest market.

sections.heading: Installed stock and annual additions differ
paragraphs: IFR’s World Robotics 2026 report puts operational industrial-robot stock in 2025 at about five million, up 9%. New installations during that year exceeded 600,000, up 11%. These measure different things and should not be used interchangeably.

sections.heading: Asia’s markets moved in different directions
paragraphs: China installed about 354,000 robots, up 20%, representing 59% of global additions. Japan installed 36,219, down 19%; South Korea about 30,000, down 1%; and India nearly 10,500, up 15%. Growth was not uniform across the region.

sections.heading: The US moves into second place
paragraphs: US installations rose 12% to nearly 38,500, overtaking Japan to become the second-largest market after China. Germany remained Europe’s largest market, but additions fell 8% to fewer than 25,000. Italy, France and Spain also declined.

sections.heading: Forecasts are not completed installations
paragraphs: IFR forecasts 655,000 installations in 2026 and 806,000 in 2029, with labor shortages and supply-chain changes supporting demand. Those figures are projections rather than already recorded deployments.

skyebrowse-crush-claims-impact-crowd-202.title: SkyeBrowse adds crash analysis and drone-based crowd counting
skyebrowse-crush-claims-impact-crowd-202.summary: New workflows connect 3D scans to vehicle-damage measurements, editable collision scenes and estimated headcounts, while retaining human review.

sections.heading: From capture to reviewable measurements
paragraphs: SkyeBrowse released Crush Analysis, Claims and Crowd Counter to extend drone and phone capture beyond 3D model creation. Measurements and reports remain linked to the model so reviewers can inspect where damage measurements originated.

sections.heading: Vehicle damage and collision scenes
paragraphs: Crush Analysis aligns a scanned vehicle with a reference model and measures six crush stations. Impact combines multiple vehicles in an editable diagram with speed estimates and an animated collision replay. Evidence and assumptions still need review; the animation is not footage of the actual crash.

sections.heading: Claims supports screening
paragraphs: Claims assesses up to eight images to suggest parts for repair, replacement or further inspection, with cost and total-loss screening. The company says licensed adjusters and policy terms determine claim outcomes.

sections.heading: Crowd counting and access
paragraphs: Crowd Counter in the SkyeBrowse Flight App on DJI RC Pro estimates people visible in a drone photograph. Standard users receive three daily counts; Public Safety & Enterprise customers receive unlimited counts. Crush Analysis and Claims are free on all plans through October 31, 2026, then included with Public Safety & Enterprise models.

skyfireai-dbox-us-autonomy-mou-2026.title: SkyfireAI and DBOX plan an integrated autonomous drone system
skyfireai-dbox-us-autonomy-mou-2026.summary: An MOU supported by Drone Nerds and XTI Aerospace targets US integration, with a demonstration planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

sections.heading: A framework for joint development
paragraphs: DRONELIFE reports that SkyfireAI and DBOX signed an MOU at the Lithuania–US Business Forum in Miami. XTI Aerospace and its Drone Nerds subsidiary helped establish the collaboration, aiming to integrate an autonomous drone operating system for the US market.

sections.heading: Complementary components
paragraphs: SkyfireAI contributes mission control, autonomy and multi-aircraft orchestration. DBOX, developed by Lithuania’s IT Logika, supplies autonomous docking infrastructure. XTI Aerospace and Drone Nerds support program leadership, integration and commercialization.

sections.heading: Testing comes before deployment
paragraphs: Initial work covers integration, testing, safety systems, relevant approvals and operator training. The companies plan a combined demonstration in the fourth quarter of 2026, targeting applications such as public safety and critical infrastructure.

sections.heading: An MOU is not a completed installation
paragraphs: The agreement supports further technical and commercial work. It does not establish that commercial deployment or beyond-visual-line-of-sight permissions are complete everywhere. The planned tests and demonstration will provide the next evidence of progress.

polyumi-vista-multimodal-demonstrations-.title: PolyUMI teaches robots with vision, touch and contact sound
polyumi-vista-multimodal-demonstrations-.summary: The open-source demonstration platform transfers a sensing finger from a wireless handheld gripper to a robot, supporting slip control and contact-rich tasks.

sections.heading: Recording more than camera images
paragraphs: The PolyUMI team released a preprint on September 24 describing a wireless handheld gripper that synchronizes wrist vision, optical touch, contact audio and motion state. It captures interaction details that an external camera may miss.

sections.heading: Sharing sensing between teaching and execution
paragraphs: The sensing finger transfers from the demonstration gripper to the robot in about ten minutes, preserving sensing geometry. Its reported parts cost is roughly $236; that is not the price of a complete robot or collection system.

sections.heading: Combining signals with VisTA
paragraphs: VisTA combines observations across sensors and time to generate actions. In a task that lets a screwdriver rotate downward before catching it, vision, touch and audio succeeded in eight of ten trials, versus two of ten with vision alone.

sections.heading: Limits of the evidence
paragraphs: Extra sensors did not improve every task. All compared methods reached at least 80% on lightbulb turning, and the slip-control comparison used only ten trials per configuration. The results do not establish long-term industrial reliability. The project provides code, explanatory figures and experiment videos for inspection.

self-adaptive-vla-hardware-shifts-2026.title: Self-Adaptive VLA uses earlier failures to handle hardware shifts
self-adaptive-vla-hardware-shifts-2026.summary: UMass Amherst and Genesis AI researchers condition robot policies on previous attempts to compensate for deployment-time hardware differences.

sections.heading: When deployment hardware differs
paragraphs: Self-Adaptive VLA, released as a preprint on September 24, addresses hardware shifts such as joint-encoder offsets and actuation bias. These differences can make a trained policy fail at precision manipulation.

sections.heading: Using previous attempts as context
paragraphs: Training deliberately injects shifts and pairs rollout information with compensated expert demonstrations. A small encoder summarizes images, robot state and actions into context. Combining context from successive attempts helps condition the next attempt; correct expert demonstrations remain the training target.

sections.heading: A new-workstation demonstration
paragraphs: In a five-episode ring-assembly demonstration, the base policy succeeded five times at the original station and zero times after transfer. One failed trial as context produced two successes; two failed trials produced five. These are results for that demonstration, not guaranteed rates at other facilities.

sections.heading: A research method with deployment limits
paragraphs: Demonstrations cover ring assembly, corn transport, marker capping and tube insertion. Adaptation occurs across attempts, rather than repairing hardware or guaranteeing immediate recovery from every failure. Deployment still requires evaluating acceptable errors and task safety.

agibot-vietnam-nic-education-raas-2026.title: AGIBOT and Vietnam NIC launch robotics education and service initiatives
agibot-vietnam-nic-education-raas-2026.summary: A Hanoi conference connected education, research labs and robot services to support Vietnam’s embodied AI ecosystem.

sections.heading: Building local capacity
paragraphs: AGIBOT and Vietnam’s National Innovation Center held a Hanoi conference on October 2, 2026 with ECOLIV and Great Education. The company reported more than 550 participants representing over 50 educational institutions and more than 20 research organizations. The initiative focuses on skills and the support needed to put robots to work locally.

sections.heading: Education meets robot services
paragraphs: The YuanSheng program connects teaching and research through curriculum development, shared laboratories, faculty training and student practice. A Robot-as-a-Service offering involves ECOLIV in local project delivery and after-sales support. The event displayed humanoid, quadruped and wheeled platforms for education and industrial applications.

sections.heading: What remains to be demonstrated
paragraphs: Combining imported robotics technology with local skills and service providers is relevant to automation adoption across Southeast Asia. Education, retail, hospitality and manufacturing are target sectors. The announcement does not establish a commercial installed fleet or measured customer returns in Vietnam; these remain outcomes to watch as the initiatives develop.

boston-dynamics-atlas-four-finger-hand-2.title: Atlas gains a four-finger hand with 13 degrees of freedom
boston-dynamics-atlas-four-finger-hand-2.summary: Boston Dynamics trades a little finger for more articulated control, tactile sensing and simulation-based training.

sections.heading: More articulation in four fingers
paragraphs: Boston Dynamics has presented an Atlas hand with four fingers and 13 degrees of freedom, up from seven in the previous design. The thumb has four degrees of freedom and the other fingers have three each. Removing the little finger reduces size, power demand and complexity while targeting a large human-hand form factor.

sections.heading: Actuation and contact sensing
paragraphs: Direct joint actuation uses a common actuator type without transmission cables crossing joints. Pressure sensors in the fingertips and palm complement joint feedback to detect contact and slipping. Demonstrations include picking, reorienting objects within the hand and operating tool triggers, capabilities that matter when a robot handles equipment built for people.

sections.heading: Learning before deployment
paragraphs: Reinforcement learning in simulation varies torque, friction and geometry to help transfer control to real hardware. The announcement concerns an improved hand and its control approach. It does not provide standardized task success rates or long-term service-life evidence demonstrating readiness for every industrial job.

runway-praxis1-world-action-model-2026.title: Runway introduces Praxis-1 to turn video learning into robot actions
runway-praxis1-world-action-model-2026.summary: The model is being tested with robotics partners, with a public open-weight release planned in the coming months.

sections.heading: Video knowledge becomes robot control
paragraphs: Runway’s Praxis-1 builds on large-scale video pretraining to select actions for physical robots. The premise is that general footage can teach object behavior and motion before adaptation to a particular task and body. This could reduce dependence on costly demonstrations collected directly with robot hardware.

sections.heading: Testing across different bodies
paragraphs: Early partners Noble Machines, Standard Bots and Ultra are testing the model on their own hardware. The examples cover two-arm manipulation, robot arms and mobile platforms, including interactions with cans and kitchen objects. These demonstrations do not establish that the policy can handle every task or unfamiliar environment.

sections.heading: Public weights are still planned
paragraphs: Access currently targets selected pre-launch partners, with a public open-weight release planned in the coming months. A cited 0.95 correlation comes from related world-model policy evaluation comparing simulated and physical results; it is not a 95% task-success rate for Praxis-1. Task-specific evidence and release conditions remain important before adoption.

innodata-vicon-motion-capture-lab-2026.title: Innodata opens a 3D motion-capture lab for robot training
innodata-vicon-motion-capture-lab-2026.summary: The New Jersey facility uses Vicon cameras to track people, robots and objects for training data and evaluation services.

sections.heading: Capturing motion directly in 3D
paragraphs: Innodata has opened a New Jersey laboratory developed with Vicon for humanoid and physical-AI data. Infrared optical cameras measure three-dimensional movement directly instead of inferring it from two-dimensional footage. The company describes sub-millimeter measurement accuracy and millisecond latency.

sections.heading: A shared frame for people and robots
paragraphs: Tracking humans, robots and handled objects in the same space connects demonstrations with object positions and machine responses. Customers can buy existing datasets, commission custom capture or bring robots for evaluation under scripted scenarios. External measurements also provide a reference against a robot’s own sensor reports.

sections.heading: Measurement is only part of validation
paragraphs: The service offers developers reference data for model training and evaluation. Camera accuracy is a measurement specification, not a robot task-success rate. Real operating conditions, differences between robot bodies and failure cases still require testing beyond the laboratory before the resulting behavior can be relied upon in deployment.

anybotics-shift-platform-launch-2026.title: ANYbotics launches Shift to connect robot inspections with maintenance
anybotics-shift-platform-launch-2026.summary: The platform combines fleet missions, contextual analysis and connections to plant maintenance systems.

sections.heading: Turning inspection into action
paragraphs: ANYbotics has introduced Shift to connect robot inspection rounds with equipment-maintenance decisions. It brings mission management, data interpretation and business-system handoffs into a common workflow. This is a separate platform launch from the previously covered ANYmal secure-door deployment at Whitegate power station.

sections.heading: Four connected modules
paragraphs: Fleet schedules and monitors missions. Insight evaluates visual, thermal, acoustic and gas readings alongside operating context such as motor load and ambient temperature. Connect sends confirmed anomalies into maintenance systems through connectors and APIs. Maps associates readings with asset identifiers and the plant hierarchy, helping teams locate the equipment requiring attention.

sections.heading: Migration and present scope
paragraphs: ANYbotics says Data Navigator will become Shift through a regular update while retaining existing data and settings. Deployment options include managed regional cloud, a customer’s cloud and on-premise installations where needed. Support for other manufacturers’ robots is a future expansion, rather than evidence of immediate compatibility with every robot brand.

lulu-odigo-62-robots-30-stores-network-2.title: LuLu activates an Odigo robot media network across 30 UAE stores
lulu-odigo-62-robots-30-stores-network-2.summary: The live network uses 62 mobile robots for shopper assistance and advertising tailored to individual stores.

sections.heading: A network now in operation
paragraphs: LuLu Retail and Kody Middle East Holding signed a retail-media partnership in Abu Dhabi. The network puts 62 AI-enabled Odigo robots across 30 LuLu stores in the United Arab Emirates. Aletihad reports that it is live, providing a concrete deployment count rather than treating an earlier rollout ambition as a newly completed fleet.

sections.heading: Shopper help and mobile advertising
paragraphs: Odigo moves autonomously through stores to support navigation, product discovery and promotions. Campaigns can be updated in real time and tailored by location, store or market. The arrangement combines customer assistance with advertising near the point of purchase and is available to brands, agencies and media buyers.

sections.heading: Results still to measure
paragraphs: The deployment offers retailers an example of robot use beyond moving goods. However, the report does not disclose advertising revenue, conversion rates or effects on store congestion. The installed fleet is evidence of adoption; it should be distinguished from unproven claims about marketing effectiveness.

mfr-posco-plate-dunnage-robot-contract-2.title: MFR wins POSCO contract for robotic steel-plate spacer placement
mfr-posco-plate-dunnage-robot-contract-2.summary: The system combines autonomous travel, 3D vision and manipulation to place wooden spacers around heavy steel plates.

sections.heading: Automating a hazardous handling step
paragraphs: MFR, a company founded by a DGIST researcher, announced on October 2 that it won a POSCO supply project for placing wooden spacers between thick steel-plate products during warehouse shipping operations. The work brings people close to heavy plates. The company describes the project as nearing final preparation for introduction at the site.

sections.heading: Navigation followed by manipulation
paragraphs: Sensor fusion and optical tracking support travel and obstacle avoidance. At the work position, AI and 3D vision identify the plate geometry and location before the arm places a spacer. An adjustable lifting mechanism and multi-axis control address higher positions. Automatic charging and wireless supervision let operators monitor from outside the hazardous area.

sections.heading: Site performance remains to be proven
paragraphs: The contract is a significant step, but it is not evidence of completed full-scale operation. MFR plans to validate safety and usefulness in the steelworks before extending the approach to heavy-load handling, large plants and specialized manufacturing. The report supplies no measured cycle time, placement-success rate or accident reduction.

primech-vision-multi-robot-platform-2026.title: Primech Vision coordinates facility workers and multiple robot types
primech-vision-multi-robot-platform-2026.summary: A Singapore headquarters pilot brings delivery, reception and cleaning robots together with HYTRON.

sections.heading: Beyond a single-purpose robot
paragraphs: Primech Holdings introduced Primech Vision on October 1, 2026 to coordinate facility personnel and multiple robot types. A pilot at its Singapore headquarters expands the company’s approach beyond HYTRON, its restroom-cleaning robot, to include delivery, reception and other cleaning robots.

sections.heading: From an issue to a tracked task
paragraphs: Robots, cameras or staff can identify facility issues. The platform converts these into tasks, assigns them to people or robotic systems, and follows execution and completion through a central interface. The aim is to give managers a site-wide view of work rather than separate status displays for individual machines.

sections.heading: Internal testing before broader rollout
paragraphs: Primech plans live demonstrations for visiting customers from Asia, Europe and the United States starting in October. Its internal pilot evaluates workflow integration and human-robot collaboration. The announcement supplies no measured savings or broad deployment results. Exception handling and handoffs to people remain practical points to assess.

harpak-ulma-hygienic-robotic-loading-202.title: Harpak-ULMA launches hygienic robot loading with shared packaging controls
harpak-ulma-hygienic-robotic-loading-202.summary: Washdown-oriented construction and Rockwell PLC motion control target simpler integration in food packaging lines.

sections.heading: A platform for food packaging
paragraphs: Harpak-ULMA introduced robotic loading for cheese, fresh meat and snacks on October 1. It locates, inspects, picks and loads products for thermoforming, flow wrapping and tray sealing. The company describes configurations reaching hundreds of packages per minute, depending on the product and layout, rather than guaranteeing that rate for every application.

sections.heading: Washdown and product handling
paragraphs: The food configuration uses open bent-plate stainless construction instead of tubular framing, with sloped drainage surfaces and accessible components. IP69K-rated components support demanding washdown. Application-specific tooling and 2D or 3D vision guide handling; product-presence, feature and defect inspection are selected according to the job.

sections.heading: A common maintenance environment
paragraphs: Robot motion is programmed directly in a Rockwell Automation PLC using Logix, shared with the packaging machines. Modular dimensions are configured during manufacture for the available space. Demonstrations are planned for PACK EXPO on October 18–21 and Automation Fair on November 16–19, 2026. Actual products and cleaning requirements still need application testing.

doordash-air-custom-delivery-drone-2026.title: DoorDash Air reveals a six-propeller delivery drone ahead of a California trial
doordash-air-custom-delivery-drone-2026.summary: The system covers aircraft, loading and dispatch; the sub-five-minute estimate comes from early testing.

sections.heading: Designing the whole delivery chain
paragraphs: DoorDash introduced its DoorDash Air system on September 30, ahead of this TechRadar report. A custom six-propeller aircraft is paired with loading infrastructure, packaging and dispatch software. A limited Northern California trial is planned with restaurants including Chipotle and Popeyes; this is not a general launch across all markets.

sections.heading: Lowering food without landing
paragraphs: The aircraft lowers packages on a line instead of routinely landing at the destination. DoorDash describes emergency-landing safeguards and slower propellers intended to reduce noise. Air-delivery eligibility also depends on weight, distance, weather and delivery conditions, rather than package dimensions alone.

sections.heading: The limits behind the headline figures
paragraphs: DoorDash estimates that about 80% of typical US restaurant orders in its studied sample meet size and weight requirements, not that 80% are deliverable every day. The sub-five-minute average comes from early restaurant-to-recipient tests and is not a guarantee including food preparation. The passing-car noise comparison is a company claim rather than an independent measurement for every neighborhood.

safeworld-seed-safety-simulation-launch-.title: Safeworld launches human simulation for robot safety testing
safeworld-seed-safety-simulation-launch-.summary: The startup emerges with more than $12 million in seed funding to test how robots respond to unpredictable human encounters.

sections.heading: A launch focused on deployment risk
paragraphs: Safeworld emerged on October 5 with more than $12 million in seed funding led by Shine Capital and a16z Speedrun. Its founders are Carnegie Mellon Safe AI researcher Ding Zhao, Kyle Wong and Simo Rachidi. Their premise is that generative robot controllers require evaluation of variable behavior, beyond checking whether a machine follows a fixed instruction.

sections.heading: Simulating people around working robots
paragraphs: The company recreates settings such as factory blind corners in tools including Genesis or MuJoCo, then runs the robot’s actual control software against simulated human encounters. Scenarios can involve people carrying boxes, kneeling, running or falling. Gritt Robotics, which develops robots for construction and solar installations, is collaborating on these safety simulations.

sections.heading: Testing is not a blanket safety guarantee
paragraphs: Operators still need to understand how well test scenarios represent their own sites and how findings inform speed, stopping distances and operating limits. Simulation can expose weaknesses without putting people at risk, but cannot establish safety in every possible situation. Safeworld is still considering a platform versus services model; the launch is not a completed certification scheme.

orbital-robotics-arkisys-iss-arm-demo-20.title: Orbital Robotics plans ISS capture and servicing demonstrations
orbital-robotics-arkisys-iss-arm-demo-20.summary: The Arkisys collaboration targets a Q3 2027 launch of scaled robotic arms for Astrobee experiments in microgravity.

sections.heading: Three demonstrations are planned
paragraphs: Seattle startup Orbital Robotics announced on October 5 that it plans to send robotic arms to the International Space Station in Q3 2027. Three demonstrations would take place roughly a month apart. Partner Arkisys would support integration and the Astrobee platform. These are future experiments, not completed satellite repairs.

sections.heading: One Astrobee would service another
paragraphs: Astronauts would install scaled versions of the company’s ORA-A arms on one free-flying Astrobee. It would capture a second Astrobee and replace a simple compute module launched for the experiment. The aim is to evaluate capture hardware and autonomous control software together in microgravity, extending laboratory testing into real spaceflight conditions.

sections.heading: A useful proxy with clear limits
paragraphs: The company says it is funding launch and demonstrations internally, with Arkisys implementing them through its NASA agreement. The arms could remain aboard for cargo handling and further research. Success would support confidence in robotic servicing, but an experiment inside the station is not equivalent to an operational mission repairing a satellite outside it.

coco-deliveroo-uk-rollout-partnership-20.title: Coco and Deliveroo announce a UK robot-delivery rollout
coco-deliveroo-uk-rollout-partnership-20.summary: The rollout starts with Canary Wharf in October and plans four further cities, while riders continue to handle most orders.

sections.heading: A staged UK introduction
paragraphs: Coco Robotics and Deliveroo announced an exclusive UK robot-delivery partnership on October 5. Canary Wharf is scheduled first in October, followed by Milton Keynes, Leeds, Stockton on Tees and Nottingham over subsequent weeks and months. The announcement describes a phased rollout, not service already operating across all five locations.

sections.heading: Local trips need local support
paragraphs: The electric sidewalk robots travel at walking pace and target short delivery journeys. Initial participating businesses include Patty&Bun, Signorelli and Beam. Expansion includes local depots, charging and maintenance operations. Deliveroo says its rider network will continue fulfilling most orders, with robots providing another option for suitable trips.

sections.heading: Sharing the sidewalk
paragraphs: Coco also plans to share detected sidewalk hazards with BlindSquare to support alerts for blind and partially sighted pedestrians. Coverage, delivery consistency and responses to blocked routes will matter as service begins. The release does not yet provide independent performance results from the planned UK operation.

ff-eai-september-265-units-report-2026.summary: The company reports 817 cumulative units and plans an October 14 education-product event; the totals cover multiple device forms.

sections.heading: Company-reported monthly totals
paragraphs: An October 5 investor release reports 265 robotics-device sales and shipments in September, 575 during Q3 and 817 from late February through September. The release combines sales and shipments in its wording. These are company-reported figures across device forms, not a count exclusively of humanoids or independently audited totals in this article.

sections.heading: Applications are at different stages
paragraphs: FF describes education and research as entering early scaled growth, security and inspection as initial proof-of-concept deployments, and industrial and logistics work as channel expansion and internal development. Commercial services are still validating operating revenue. Those stages matter: aggregate device totals do not establish mature deployment in every application.

sections.heading: An event and a proposed transaction
paragraphs: FFAI and FFR plan an October 14 Pacific Time event for education-related EAI Brain, Skills and device products, including the Physical AI Spark Program. The transfer of the robotics business to FFR remains a proposed transaction subject to completion. Planned products and restructuring should be distinguished from reported activity; the company’s market-ranking claims are not independently verified here.

sections.heading: Connecting three disciplines
paragraphs: ARC Singapore launched on October 5 to connect AI developers, robotics suppliers, cybersecurity specialists, researchers and enterprise users. Its premise is that decision software, physical machines and connected networks must be assessed together when AI controls work in real environments.

sections.heading: A regional network is planned
paragraphs: The body signed MoUs with chapter leads in Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam. Planned work covers policy input, cross-sector collaboration, digital trust and skills development. First-year working groups include an AI risk framework jointly led by a solution provider and an enterprise user.

sections.heading: Implications for system buyers
paragraphs: For Thai businesses, the potential value is closer regional alignment between automation procurement and security evaluation. However, these agreements do not create binding standards or certify products. Proposed trust baselines and procurement guidance remain development goals whose practical value will depend on published documents and implementation.

minerva-roger-preseed-hazardous-work-202.title: Minerva unveils Roger for hazardous work with $10 million in funding
minerva-roger-preseed-hazardous-work-202.summary: Roger combines AI-assisted mobility with specialist control through VR, with paid pilots planned for the fall.

sections.heading: Funding supports initial field pilots
paragraphs: Minerva Humanoids emerged on October 6 with approximately $10 million in pre-seed funding led by General Catalyst, with Long Journey Ventures and Credo Ventures as co-leads. Roger targets hazardous onshore and offshore energy work and public-safety applications. The company plans its first paid pilots for the fall.

sections.heading: Specialists retain critical control
paragraphs: Roger is semi-autonomous. Minerva Intelligence manages balance, fall recovery and navigation while translating remote operator input into movement. A specialist uses a VR headset to see through the robot and perform fine manipulation. The intended model preserves human judgment for critical actions rather than giving a robot independent authority over hazardous work.

sections.heading: A prototype is not broad deployment
paragraphs: Minerva says it developed a walking prototype in five months. Initial units are manufactured and assembled in Germany, with production planned in Germany and the US. Rapid development does not establish reliability in every field condition. Pilot results will need to demonstrate communication quality, controllability and resilience as operating environments change.

yyforce-singapore-robotics-training-cent.title: YYForce opens Singapore center for service-robot training
yyforce-singapore-robotics-training-cent.summary: The center collects operational data and tests human–robot workflows while evaluating leasing and robotics-as-a-service models.

sections.heading: A service-workflow test center
paragraphs: YYForce announced the opening of its Robotics Training, Data and Experience Center in Singapore on October 6. It supports humanoid training, operational data collection, workflow testing and customer demonstrations for hospitality, cleaning, security, delivery and facility management, drawing on the company’s existing workforce services.

sections.heading: Learning from simulated workplaces
paragraphs: Test environments cover housekeeping, restroom cleaning, banqueting and hospitality support. Data includes navigation, motion, object interaction and environmental conditions. The center evaluates collaboration between people, humanoids and specialized robots. A security command center also demonstrates patrol robots integrated with cameras, sensors and central monitoring.

sections.heading: Commercial capability remains under evaluation
paragraphs: YYForce explicitly says training does not establish autonomous completion of full housekeeping or restroom-cleaning duties. It is assessing RaaS, leasing and managed-service arrangements but has not announced material robotics orders or recurring revenue from these proposed models. Viability depends on productivity, service quality, maintenance costs and required human intervention.

exotec-first-supply-next-morning-results.title: First Supply reports Skypod results supporting next-morning delivery
exotec-first-supply-next-morning-results.summary: The company-reported results describe 10-times-faster picking and more than 14,000 SKUs after over a year of operation.

sections.heading: Results after more than a year
paragraphs: Exotec published First Supply’s Skypod operating results on October 6, after more than a year of use. The reported service milestone is next-morning delivery for orders placed by 5 p.m. First Supply distributes HVAC, plumbing, lighting and industrial products whose availability affects contractors’ schedules.

sections.heading: Picking performance and storage headroom
paragraphs: The release reports more than 14,000 SKUs in the system and picking speeds ten times those of previous manual processes. Vertical storage reduces operator travel. Fourfold storage-capacity growth within the existing racking footprint is expansion potential, not an already completed fourfold increase. These figures are supplier-and-customer claims rather than an independent benchmark.

sections.heading: Service outcomes matter alongside speed
paragraphs: First Supply says next-day demand can represent up to 20% of daily distribution-center volume, making overnight replenishment operationally important. However, the announcement does not detail the tenfold comparison methodology or total costs needed for a payback calculation. Other operators should compare the case with their own product mix and peak-demand patterns.

robco-billion-valuation-alfie-launch-pla.title: RobCo reaches billion-dollar valuation ahead of planned Alfie launch
robco-billion-valuation-alfie-launch-pla.summary: The transaction combines new investment with an employee secondary sale as RobCo expands US operations and prepares its industrial robot.

sections.heading: Valuation is different from capital raised
paragraphs: RobCo’s valuation exceeded $1 billion in a transaction first reported on October 5 and covered by Modern Materials Handling on October 6. It combines investment in the company with a secondary share sale for employees. The valuation is not a billion-dollar fundraising amount. Participants include existing investors such as Sequoia and Lightspeed and new investors including Cherry Ventures.

sections.heading: Alfie is scheduled for 2027
paragraphs: RobCo plans Alfie’s commercial launch at its RobCoN summit in Munich on March 4, 2027. The company describes an industrial robot combining perception, reasoning and execution for variable factory tasks. That is a product positioning and development goal, not independent proof that it can handle every industrial workflow without preparation.

sections.heading: US operations are expanding
paragraphs: The company reports customer operations across more than a dozen states, manufacturing and assembly in Austin, and a San Francisco lab. CEO Roman Hölzl has relocated to the US. Local operations may support deployment and service, but practical value still depends on application reliability, safety and total costs. The announced commercial launch remains a future milestone.

boston-dynamics-rohit-prasad-ceo-2026.title: Boston Dynamics appoints Rohit Prasad CEO effective October 7
boston-dynamics-rohit-prasad-ceo-2026.summary: The former Amazon AI leader will guide the company’s integration of AI and robotics and its commercialization efforts.

sections.heading: A leadership change takes effect
paragraphs: Boston Dynamics announced on October 6 that Rohit Prasad will become chief executive officer effective October 7, 2026. The stated focus is integrating advanced AI with robotics and expanding commercial applications. This is a distinct corporate development from the previously covered Atlas hand announcement.

sections.heading: Experience in AI product development
paragraphs: Prasad previously served as an Amazon senior vice president and head scientist for Alexa and Artificial General Intelligence. During twelve years there he helped develop Alexa and later the Amazon Nova foundation-model family. Earlier, he spent nearly fourteen years at Raytheon BBN Technologies working on machine learning and its applications.

sections.heading: Strategy does not establish new capabilities
paragraphs: Boston Dynamics identifies Spot for inspection, Stretch for box handling and electric Atlas as a platform in development. The leadership announcement gives no new product delivery schedule or demonstrated technical capability. Prasad’s expected board appointment remains subject to approval. Commercial and technical progress must therefore be assessed separately from the strategic intent of the hire.
